rationale.idea: Add a train-only item-item co-watch affinity reranker on top of the incumbent FM+BPR scores and tune only the blend weight on validation.
rationale.why_expected_to_help: The FM baseline ranks from user/item/context feature interactions but does not explicitly exploit sparse item-item collaborative transitions from a user’s past positive watches to current candidates. Summed normalized co-watch affinity varies within a user’s candidate list, so it can directly reorder impressions and potentially rescue mistakes where semantically related videos share audiences despite weak tabular overlap. Because this is an additive broad signal rather than a reweighting or concentrated sampling change, it follows the dataset’s observed winning pattern more closely than prior failed signal-concentration interventions.
rationale.grounded_in: Grounded in the measured project pattern that 'broad additive signal has won' while 'every intervention that CONCENTRATED or REWEIGHTED the training signal lost', plus the user_history axis description noting that each user has hundreds of train interactions and history remains a top-ranked open direction. Mechanistically this is closest to classic item-item collaborative filtering via cosine-normalized co-occurrence (Sarwar et al., WWW 2001), but applied strictly as a train-only post-hoc within-user reranker.

code_summary: Train the incumbent menu configuration once via train_lib.run to get base valid/test scores, then compute an item-item co-watch affinity matrix from TRAIN long_view positives only. For each user, build a history of positively long-viewed train videos and score each valid/test candidate by the sum of normalized co-occurrence affinities from that history to the candidate video. Standardize the affinity term on each split and blend it additively with the base FM score using a small fixed sweep of alpha chosen on VALID only. This cannot be expressed by existing menu primitives because it is neither a built-in architecture, loss, nor user-history encoder inside training; it is a post-hoc collaborative reranker over the scored candidate list.
